title: Gateway token-priority misassignment caused client surge; implement deterministic backoff & reconciler
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-04 a misassignment of token priority metadata in the gateway led to incorrect quota attributions for ~3% of active tokens, allowing a subset of clients to bypass expected burst controls. The result was a concentrated surge of concurrent requests to inference hosts, producing transient 503s for ~120 customers and 429 spikes for adjacent rate-limited tenants. This ticket captures the investigation, short-term mitigations applied, and the plan for durable fixes.
timeline:
2026-03-04 08:14 UTC — First alert: latency SLOs breached for API-gateway-prod route.
2026-03-04 08:18 UTC — Dashboard shows token-level concurrency skew concentrated in us-west-2.
2026-03-04 08:23 UTC — Emergency triage: initial hypothesis of upstream client bug.
2026-03-04 08:31 UTC — Live trace shows token metadata 'priority' field set to 'vip' for unrelated accounts.
2026-03-04 08:45 UTC — Applied near-term mitigation: temporary hard cap on per-tenant concurrent requests at gateway layer.
2026-03-04 09:10 UTC — Error budget alerts returned to normal for majority of tenants.
2026-03-04 12:00 UTC — Root cause confirmed: race in token-decorators service where async refresh could overwrite cached priority on token rebind.

2026-03-06 02:00 UTC — Reconciler fully rolled out and monitoring shows stable concurrency distribution.

root_cause: A race condition in token-decorators (introduced during a prior optimization to reduce blocking calls) allowed an async refresh path to write stale or defaulted priority values into the shared token cache. This occasionally overwrote authoritative assignments coming from the auth service, causing some tokens to be treated as high-priority and bypass soft burst controls. The bug was not caught by existing unit tests because they assumed single-threaded cache updates; integration tests did not simulate the refresh timing profile seen in production under heavy churn.
mitigations: Short-term: enforced a hard per-tenant concurrent-request cap at the gateway (applied 08:45 UTC) to arrest surge patterns.
Medium-term: added a deterministic reconciler that validates token metadata against auth-service authoritative copy and corrects cache entries on detection.
Monitoring: created a new alert on token-priority drift where >0.5% of tokens for a tenant have 'priority' values that don't match recent auth events.
Customer comms: notified affected customers via status.redwood.ai incident page and opened follow-up tickets for high-impact accounts.
action_items: ENG-60878: Add deterministic backoff + jittered retry logic to gateway request admission to prevent synchronized retries (owner: Marco, estimate: 3).
ENG-60879: Harden token-decorators cache writes with compare-and-swap (CAS) semantics and re-run concurrency integration tests (owner: Priya Mehta, estimate: 5).
ENG-60900: Create an end-to-end chaos test that simulates auth refresh storms and validates cache consistency across token-decorators, gateway, and auth-service (owner: SRE team, estimate: 4).
ENG-60901: Ship an observability dashboard widget that surfaces token-level attribution heatmaps and a daily report to identify early drift (owner: Observability, estimate: 2).

ENG-60902: Update runbook 'gateway-rate-incidents' with playbook step for applying temporary per-tenant caps and steps to rollback reconciler if it causes unexpected churn (owner: Oncall Lead, estimate: 1).
ENG-60903: Postmortem blameless review and lessons learned session scheduled for 2026-03-22 (owner: Aisha, estimate: 1).
